pages.title: Getting consent
pages.subtitle: What carriers expect before you send a financial services text.

blocks.heading: Why financial messaging gets extra scrutiny

paragraphs.text: Financial services is one of the most closely watched categories in business texting. Carriers filter it harder than almost anything else, and a single word in one message can get a campaign suspended.
what you can send from a 10DLC number, the language that triggers filtering, and the consent setup carriers expect — so your messages land and your account stays in good standing.

blocks.heading: Get consent right
blocks.intro: Every contact must have verifiable, specific consent on file before you send.

rows.definition: Collect explicit, checkbox-based opt-in with fully compliant disclosure language.
Each use case — transactional and informational — needs its own checkbox.
State that mobile numbers, SMS consent and message data are never sold or shared.
Store timestamped records for every contact and keep them for at least four years.

blocks.title: Need form wording and disclosure language?
blocks.text: Form wording, disclosure placement, and privacy-policy language are covered step by step in the SMS Opt-In Compliance Guide — ask your Salesmsg team for a copy.

pages.title: What to include,
pages.subtitle: Required content in every message and practices that trigger carrier filtering.

blocks.heading: What to put in every message

rows.definition: Account updates, payment confirmations, appointment reminders and service notifications are safest.
Identify your company by name in every initial message you send.
Include opt-out instructions in every initial message.
Include "Reply STOP to unsubscribe" in every broadcast you send.

blocks.heading: What to avoid
blocks.intro: Any of these practices can get a campaign suspended.

rows.definition: Contacts need verifiable proof: a web form, keyword opt-in or verbal consent.
Each message type needs its own checkbox; bundling is noncompliant.
Any policy mentioning sharing or selling consumer data makes you noncompliant.
Never send before 8:00 AM or after 9:00 PM recipient local time.
Carrier fines range from $1,000 to $10,000+ per violation.
Loan or financial product promotions require an approved short code.

blocks.title: URL shorteners must be branded
blocks.text: Public shorteners like bit.ly or tinyurl are prohibited. Use company-branded short links only.

pages.subtitle: Terms flagged by carriers and Twilio as high-risk financial content.

paragraphs.text: solicits, arranges, brokers, refers, refinances or markets new loans is prohibited by mobile carriers. Using flagged terms can trigger filtering, campaign suspension or fines of $1,000–$10,000+ per violation.

rows.label: Lead generation
rows.note: "based on your profile", "on behalf of", "affiliate offer"

blocks.title: Search your saved content first
blocks.text: Flagged terms appear in templates, automations, broadcasts and signature lines you set up months ago. Search your saved content before you scale up sending.

blocks.heading: Before you send
blocks.intro: Run through this checklist before every campaign launch.

rows.definition: Separate checkbox per message type; timestamped records retained four years.
Confirms data is not sold or shared with third parties.
Company name and opt-out in every initial message; no flagged wording.
Scheduled 8:00 AM–9:00 PM recipient local time.

blocks.title: Not sure a message will pass?
blocks.text: Send it to your Salesmsg team first. We'd rather review it now than untangle a filtered campaign later.
